thread:
anya: Quick live thread from today's runtime roadmap segment. Post follow-ups, clarifications, or things you want us to action.

raj: Thanks. Can you recap the rollout cadence for the batching changes again? I missed the timeline.

anya: Sure — canary this week for internal clusters, limited external canary next week, GA by end of month if no regressions. Exact dates posted to the release board.

sam: For the external canary we'll limit to low-traffic routes and add an opt-in flag per-tenant. We'll also enable tracing spans that show batch fill percentage.

liam: Performance goal: 15-25% token-cost reduction for standard chat workloads and 10-20% throughput lift for GPU-backed hosts. p99 target remains <= 150ms for 2k request mix on our n1/p4 configs.

julie: Any known memory tradeoffs with the new prefix KV caching policy? We had a spike last trial.

sam: The new policy introduces an LRU-with-decay and a hard per-worker cap. We also added a diagnostic metric `kv_cache_reserved_bytes` so ops can see how close clusters are to cap. That should prevent unexpected OOMs.

raj: Where will customers see the new metrics? Console or API?

liam: Both. Console charts for kv hit-rate, `batch_fill_pct`, and `avg_batch_latency_ms`. API exposes raw counters for historical analysis and Optimize will surface cost deltas if you run a simulator.

deploy-bot: deploy: scheduled canary deployment queued for cluster "int-canary-2" — ETA 40m.

julie: Kernel question: are fused attention kernels enabled by default anywhere? We had a bug in our plugin last sprint.

liam: Not by default on Hosted. They're behind `kernels.fused_attention` feature flag. Dedicated customers can opt-in per-cluster. We've gated them until the Ampere codegen corner is fixed.

ops-bot: alert: increased variance observed in short-sequence quantized runs on ampere-testbed-4. Investigation ongoing.

sam: We're tracking a ~6% regression on sequences < 32 tokens with the quantized path. Kernel team has a microkernel tweak that looks promising; plan to test tonight.

anya: Action item — sam, add a short note in the canary playbook about the short-seq regression and a suggested fallback config (`kernel_version: "safe-quant"`) for latency-sensitive routes.

sam: Will do. Also adding a quick example config for customers to try:

```json
{
  "opt_in_kernels": "fused-attn-v2",
  "max_batch_latency_ms": 8,
  "min_batch_size": 2,
  "kv_mem_quota": "4GB"
}
```

raj: Nice. For the evictions, are we favoring longer-running prefixes or most-recently-used? Which yields better hit rate for chat sessions?

liam: We bias towards longer-lived prefixes (session-aware) because chat throughput benefits from keeping the head contexts cached. For stateless workloads MRU works better; we plan to make the policy pluggable per-route.

julie: How will rollbacks work if we see quality regressions? You mentioned eval hooks.

sam: Rollout controller can run evals as part of a canary step. If an eval metric crosses threshold, it auto-pauses and posts results to the runbook channel, and we can auto-rollback after manual confirmation.

anya: We'll also publish a customer-facing note summarizing the opt-in risks/benefits and suggested knobs for latency-first vs cost-first apps.

deploy-bot: canary: job started on int-canary-2.

raj: One last ask — could we schedule a short office hours for customers to walk through the Optimize sim results? A few teams asked.

anya: Yes, we'll run two sessions next week; I’ll post invites and a signup form.

sam: I'll be online for the canary window tonight if folks want to watch traces with me. Ping @sam.

anya: Great thread — I'll follow up with links to the canary dashboard, the canary playbook, and a gist with the example configs. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
